subject: Price stability & retroactive rebate pathway for renewal - Acme Ops
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Jenna Park <jenna.park@acmeops.com>, Tomás Rivera <tomas.rivera@acmeops.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Price stability & retroactive rebate pathway for renewal - Acme Ops

Hi Jenna / Tomás,

Thanks again for the thoughtful conversation last week. Per our roadmap review and your usage trend, I wanted to put a concise proposal on the table to clear the renewal path and give you short-term price stability while we onboard the additional capacity you requested. High level:

- Term: 24 months (auto-renew option)
- Commit: convert current retainer to a 25% uplift in committed capacity (applies to Dedicated pool hours)
- Discount: 10% off list for committed tiers for the first 12 months
- Price hold: 6-month absolute price hold on the committed SKU after signature
- Retroactive rebate: for overage incurred in Q2 2027 (Apr–Jun), Redwood will apply a one-time rebate up to $35,000 against future invoices if the overage is caused by onboarding burst or platform migration patterns we scoped together. Conditions and calculation in attached workbook.

Attached: ACME_Rate_Model_v2.xlsx (model with examples and credit math).

Ask: Can you confirm whether Procurement wants the rebate language as a separate credit schedule or embedded in the MSA addendum? Also, are your legal / procurement folks available for a 30-minute call next week (propose Tue 10–11am PT)?

If you prefer, we can offer an alternative where we reduce the initial discount to 8% and increase the rebate cap to $50k — happy to discuss tradeoffs.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0132

[attachment: ACME_Rate_Model_v2.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]
From: Jenna Park <jenna.park@acmeops.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tomás Rivera <tomas.rivera@acmeops.com>, Procurement <procurement@acmeops.com>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Price stability & retroactive rebate pathway for renewal - Acme Ops

Naomi —

Thanks for the clear proposal and the model. A couple of quick clarifying items from Procurement and our ops team:

1) Retroactive rebate: procurement wants the rules for the rebate to be deterministic — will the credit be limited to usage directly attributable to migration/onboarding as you note, and what evidence will Redwood accept?

2) Scope: does the commit uplift and discount apply only to Dedicated capacity or to Hosted API usage as well? We may split workloads across both.

3) Timing & docs: Procurement prefers the rebate as an appendix to the MSA rather than a separate PO addendum. They also asked for DocuSign-ready language and a draft SOW.

We think the alternative you proposed (8% + $50k rebate cap) might be closer to what leadership will sign quickly — can you quantify the NPV difference in the workbook? Also, please share a short executive note summarizing customer impact and why we should accept the rebate structure.

Available Tue 10–11am PT for the call.

—Jenna
Jenna Park
Head of Ops | Acme Ops
jenna.park@acmeops.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Acme — pricing approach and negotiation levers

Folks —

Quick internal plan before we hop on the call with Jenna:

- Position A (preferred): 10% for 12 months + $35k rebate cap; preserves margin and keeps price hold limited to 6 months. Makes it easy to transition them to committed billing.
- Position B (compromise): 8% + $50k rebate cap (as Naomi floated) — gives them more downside protection, higher rebate budget but slightly lower margin.
- Concession we can make later: convert some portion of rebate to an upfront credit against the first invoice to reduce perceived risk on their side.

Ben: can you run the model with both scenarios and include a column showing gross margin impact and payback time?

I’ll draft a one-page exec note focused on customer reliability during migration and retention risk if we push too hard on price.

Marissa
Head of Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jenna Park <jenna.park@acmeops.com>, Tomás Rivera <tomas.rivera@acmeops.com>
Date: Wed, 26 May 2027 11:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Price stability & retroactive rebate pathway for renewal - Acme Ops

Team / Jenna —

Attached is a revised credit schedule and sensitivity table: ACME_Credit_Schedule.pdf. Key ask: we can accept the 8% discount with a $25k upfront credit applied at invoice 1 + a supplemental retroactive rebate cap of $25k (so total program protection up to $50k if both apply). We recommend making the rebate contingent on a short onboarding runbook (dates and traffic patterns) and usage logs to be shared by Acme Ops.

Operational details:
- Discount: 8% applied to committed tiers for 12 months
- Upfront credit: $25,000 applied on the first invoice as a line-item credit (reduces initial cash flow friction for Acme)
- Retro rebate: up to $25,000 applied as bill credits for verified overage in Q2 2027; combined program limit $50,000
- Price hold: 60 days after signature for the committed SKU; during that time we will not raise list rates for the committed tier.

We believe this preserves enough margin while giving Acme immediate relief and a meaningful runway during migration. If Procurement insists on the rebate being embedded in the MSA, we will provide exact contract language for the credit schedule.

Ben Carter
Commercial Operations | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

Ben / Naomi —

This looks reasonable. Procurement will accept the credit breakdown as an MSA appendix if you provide the DocuSign-ready language and the upfront credit as a line item. Leadership is asking for a one-paragraph executive summary that articulates: why Redwood is making the concession, how this mitigates Acme’s risk during migration, and the expected timeline for normalizing to committed billing.

If you can get that note to me by EOD Monday, I can escalate internally and we should be able to sign within 5 business days.

—Jenna

Date: Wed, 9 Jun 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Price stability & retroactive rebate pathway for renewal - Acme Ops

Jenna —

Thanks — attached is the one-paragraph executive summary and the DocuSign-ready credit appendix link. If Procurement confirms the appendix language, we will issue the first-invoice credit within 5 business days of signing and lock the 60-day price-hold.

Executive summary (for leadership):
Redwood is offering a short-term, targeted relief package to de-risk Acme Ops' migration to committed capacity. The package balances revenue predictability with operational support: an 8% introductory discount on committed tiers, a $25k upfront credit to reduce initial cash impact, and a supplementary retroactive rebate program (up to $25k) to cover verified migration-driven overage. Combined protections total up to $50k. This approach removes immediate pricing uncertainty during onboarding while preserving our long-term unit economics and incentivizing a conversion to committed billing.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/DocuSignLink/ACME-Renewal-2027
HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.company/acmeops/deal/ACME-2027-RNWL-42

Please reply with a confirmation line so we can route the MSA appendix to legal for finalization.

Best,
Naomi
